title: Feasibility and Safety of an AI Chatbot Compared to Self-Help Materials for University Student Well-Being: A Pilot Study
official: Agentic GenAI-Enabled Psychotherapeutic Interventions for Well-Being: A Pilot Research Study of Feasibility and Safety
summary:
The goal of this Pilot study is to examine the possibility and safety of using Artificial Intelligence (AI) conversational tools (chatbots) to help improve individuals' mental well-being. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* How safe is an AI chatbot in use for a study about mental wellness?
* How usable is the platform for this study?
* How willing are participants to remain and complete the study?
* What was the user experience like?
* Do they show any signs of dependancy on the chatbot?

Researchers will compare participants who did the mental wellness sessions with the chosen chatbot, Doro, to those who used common self-help materials to examine the safety and effectiveness of AI chatbots in supporting mental wellness.

Participants will:

* Have a pre-study mental wellness assessment.
* Be divided into 2 groups: the experimental group and the control group.
* The experimental group will interact with the Doro AI Chatbot.
* The control group will interact with the self-help work materials.
* Have a mid-point mental wellness assessment.
* Have a mental wellness survey after all the sessions, and
* Have a final interview with one of the researchers.

interventions.name: Self-help reading materials with reflection exercises

criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Currently enrolled as a student at the University of Waterloo
* Age 17 or older
* Kessler Psychological Distress Scale (K10) score between 10 and 30 points
* World Health Organization Well-Being Index (WHO-5) score of 28% or above and below 80%
* Possesses a device on which the study platform can be accessed

Exclusion Criteria:

* Change in the last month or planned changes in mental health treatment during the study period (starting therapy, counselling, or medication, or modifying current treatment)
* Kessler Psychological Distress Scale (K10) score above 30 points, or WHO-5 score below 28%
* Very low psychological distress (K10 score below 10 or WHO-5 score of above 80%)
